name: Great Schism Between Rome and Constantinople
summary: Cardinal Humbert of Silva Candida places a bull of excommunication on the altar of Hagia Sophia, excommunicating Patriarch Michael I Cerularius of Constantinople. Cerularius excommunicates the papal legates. The mutual excommunications formalize centuries of theological and political divergence over papal supremacy, the Filioque clause, celibacy, and liturgical differences.

_quarry.structural_significance: Creates the permanent split between Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Christianity; shapes the political and cultural divide between Western and Eastern Europe; not formally lifted until 1965 when Paul VI and Athenagoras I revoked the mutual excommunications.
